mechanism: FTSE Russell US index reconstitutions publish membership changes before a fixed effective close. Passive products and benchmark-constrained portfolios must realign holdings to the reconstituted benchmark, concentrating non-informational demand and supply into the effective close/closing-auction mechanism. The December 2026 semi-annual reconstitution creates a second annual implementation clock under the new 2026 schedule.
claim: A rules-based Russell US reconstitution creates a causally explicit benchmark-tracking flow at the announced effective close. A later, separately authorized economic test could ask whether supplying liquidity to sufficiently large predicted benchmark demand/supply has a repeatable capturable concession after auction mechanics, anticipatory trading, spread, impact, borrow and crowding; no return effect is claimed here.
prediction: Before any candidate return data are inspected, documentary evidence should establish a rank/reference clock, preliminary membership publication, an effective close, affected benchmark weights/universe, and a material population of benchmarked/passive assets whose tracking constraint implies implementation demand. Failure to establish ex-ante membership/weight deltas or a genuine implementation obligation blocks test design.
falsification_scope: Mechanism usability is falsified if benchmark changes cannot be reconstructed point-in-time before the effective close, if passive/benchmark implementation is too discretionary to imply a dated flow, or if closing-auction liquidity mechanically absorbs the relevant flow without a measurable pre-specified execution concession. A later negative economic test would falsify only its frozen expression, not the existence of benchmark-tracking trades.

decision_map.forced_actor: Passive Russell-index products and benchmark-constrained portfolios that seek to minimize tracking error at the reconstitution effective close.
decision_map.constraint: Holdings must reflect announced index membership/weights when the reconstituted index becomes effective; implementation is naturally concentrated at the official closing price used for index transition.
decision_map.clock: For the second 2026 Russell US reconstitution: Rank Day 2026-10-30; preliminary additions/deletions 2026-11-13; query period 2026-11-16 through 2026-11-27; lockdown begins 2026-11-30; changes take effect after the US close 2026-12-11; reconstituted indexes operate from 2026-12-14.
decision_map.affected_universe: Russell US index additions, deletions and size-index membership movements, with exact eligible names/weights to be frozen only from point-in-time FTSE Russell publications before outcome access.
decision_map.capacity_intuition: Potentially material gross flow because FTSE Russell reports trillions of dollars benchmarked to Russell US indexes, but capacity for any liquidity-supply expression may be sharply reduced by deep closing-auction liquidity, anticipatory arbitrage and crowding.
implementability_questions: Can preliminary/final constituent files and weight inputs be archived point-in-time with publication timestamps?
Can expected passive share demand/supply be computed from benchmark weights and benchmarked passive AUM without using post-event prices?
Which names have sufficient auction liquidity relative to predicted benchmark flow under a frozen capacity rule?
Can NYSE closing auctions and Nasdaq Closing Cross execution assumptions be represented without using hindsight fills?
How should query-period membership changes be handled without post-outcome selection?
Can borrow, spread, auction imbalance access and impact assumptions be frozen before any economic outcome inspection?
active_disconfirmation: FTSE Russell deliberately publishes preliminary lists and repeated updates before implementation, giving arbitrageurs time to pre-position and potentially eliminating any concession.

The provider reports very large reconstitution-close trading volumes, and primary exchange closing auctions/Closing Cross are designed to concentrate liquidity, which may absorb benchmark flow efficiently.
The mechanism may therefore be structurally real while offering no residual economic rent after crowding and impact; validation must not equate forced flow with alpha.

primary_documentary_evidence.source: FTSE Russell / LSEG — December 2026 Russell US Indexes Reconstitution schedule
primary_documentary_evidence.fact: Confirms 2026-10-30 Rank Day, 2026-11-13 preliminary lists, query and lockdown periods, and 2026-12-11 effective close.

primary_documentary_evidence.source: FTSE Russell / LSEG — June 2026 semi-annual reconstitution
primary_documentary_evidence.fact: Documents point-in-time preliminary/update schedule, effective close, approximately $12.2T benchmarked/invested assets, large reconstitution-close trading, and use of NYSE closing auction / Nasdaq Closing Cross.

primary_documentary_evidence.source: FTSE Russell / LSEG — semi-annual frequency decision
primary_documentary_evidence.fact: Documents benchmark/passive scale and the move to semi-annual reconstitution from 2026.

nearby_but_distinct: month-end pension rebalance: asset-allocation rebalance proxy rather than constituent-level benchmark membership implementation
NASDAQ/NDX short-horizon reversal: generic index reversal rather than announced benchmark reconstitution flow
ADR termination forced sale: depositary residual inventory rather than benchmark tracking

next_validator_decision.PASS_TO_TEST_DESIGN: Point-in-time constituent/weight files, implementation clock and benchmark-flow sizing inputs can be frozen before any price/return access.
next_validator_decision.PARK_DATA: Mechanism is real but required historical point-in-time membership/weight or auction data cannot be reconstructed without leakage/private data.
next_validator_decision.KILL_MECHANISM: Benchmark implementation is not sufficiently constrained/datable or the proposed flow proxy cannot be specified independently of outcomes.
